## General information 2

# Special Words Definition

## Batting Average
- Batting average is a measure of a batsman's performance, calculated by dividing the total number of runs scored by the number of times they have been dismissed. A higher batting average indicates a more consistent and successful batsman.
- Batting Average = Total Runs ÷ Total Dismissals

## Strike Rate
- In batting, strike rate indicates the scoring rate of a batsman, showing the average number of runs scored per 100 balls faced. A higher strike rate reflects an aggressive and fast-scoring batsman.
- Strike Rate = (Total Runs ÷ Balls Faced) × 100

## Wickets Taken
- Wickets taken refers to the total number of times a bowler has successfully dismissed an opposing batsman. This statistic is a core measure of a bowler's effectiveness and impact on the game.

## Economy Rate
- Economy rate measures a bowler's efficiency by indicating the average number of runs conceded per over (6 balls) bowled. A lower economy rate shows greater control and efficiency in restricting the opposition's scoring.
- Economy Rate = (Total Runs Conceded ÷ Balls Bowled) × 6

## Wickets Taken
- The number of times a bowler successfully dismisses a batsman in a single match.  This metric is a direct indicator of the bowler's effectiveness, showing how many players they were able to remove from play.

## Runs Given
- The total number of runs scored by the batting side off a particular bowler’s deliveries in a single match.  This value reflects the runs the bowler has conceded to the batting team, and a lower runs-given value is typically favorable for the bowler's performance.

Calculate the total number of wickets taken by each bowler (excluding run-outs and other dismissals not attributed to the bowler), their economy rate (total runs conceded divided by total overs bowled, considering only runs scored off the bat and ignoring any extra runs like wides and no-balls), their strike rate (average number of balls bowled per wicket taken), and their best bowling performance in a single match (the match with the most wickets taken by the bowler, formatted as "wickets-runs" where runs are the runs conceded excluding extras).

First, I'll calculate each bowler's total wickets, excluding dismissals not credited to them. Next, I'll determine the total runs conceded and balls bowled for each bowler. Then, I'll find each bowler's best performance in a single match. Finally, I will join these results to compute the economy rate, strike rate, and format the best bowling performance as requested.

args.sql:
WITH BowlerWickets AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler AS player_id,
        COUNT(w.player_out) AS total_wickets
    FROM ipl.main.ball_by_ball AS b
    JOIN ipl.main.wicket_taken AS w ON b.match_id = w.match_id AND b.over_id = w.over_id AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
    WHERE w.kind_out NOT IN ('run out', 'retired hurt', 'obstructing the field')
    GROUP BY b.bowler
),
BowlerStats AS (
    SELECT 
        b.bowler AS player_id,
        COUNT(b.ball_id) AS balls_bowled,
        SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0)) AS runs_conceded
    FROM ipl.main.ball_by_ball AS b
    LEFT JOIN ipl.main.batsman_scored AS bs ON b.match_id = bs.match_id AND b.over_id = bs.over_id AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.bowler
),
MatchStats AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler AS player_id,
        b.match_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN w.kind_out NOT IN ('run out', 'retired hurt', 'obstructing the field') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets,
        SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0)) AS runs
    FROM ipl.main.ball_by_ball AS b
    LEFT JOIN ipl.main.wicket_taken AS w ON b.match_id = w.match_id AND b.over_id = w.over_id AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
    LEFT JOIN ipl.main.batsman_scored AS bs ON b.match_id = bs.match_id AND b.over_id = bs.over_id AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.bowler, b.match_id
),
BestBowling AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        wickets,
        runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY wickets DESC, runs ASC) as rn
    FROM MatchStats
)
SELECT
    p.player_name AS bowler,
    COALESCE(bw.total_wickets, 0) AS total_wickets,
    CASE WHEN bs.balls_bowled > 0 THEN ROUND(bs.runs_conceded * 6.0 / bs.balls_bowled, 2) ELSE 0 END AS economy_rate,
    CASE WHEN bw.total_wickets > 0 THEN ROUND(bs.balls_bowled * 1.0 / bw.total_wickets, 2) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate,
    COALESCE(CAST(bb.wickets AS VARCHAR) || '-' || CAST(bb.runs AS VARCHAR), '0-0') AS best_bowling
FROM ipl.main.player AS p
LEFT JOIN BowlerWickets AS bw ON p.player_id = bw.player_id
LEFT JOIN BowlerStats AS bs ON p.player_id = bs.player_id
LEFT JOIN BestBowling AS bb ON p.player_id = bb.player_id AND bb.rn = 1
WHERE bs.balls_bowled > 0
ORDER BY total_wickets DESC, economy_rate ASC;
